newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Dennis Eck, who took over as head of Coles Myer Ltd at the beginning of this year, said yesterday his company was operating as a "failed merger". Meanwhile, in his first speech since assuming his position as the chief executive of David Jones Ltd, Peter Wlkinson said "department stores have been to blame for their decline". Both men said their groups faced difficulties overcoming past mistakes and surviving one of their toughest periods. Page 1.

Austrade is hosting executives from five large Chinese companies who are in Australia looking for investment options this week. The executives are all from the Shanghai area and are interested in many areas such as building materials, metal manufacturing nd building technologies. The visit is seen as an indication of the improving relationship between Australia and China. Page 5.

Network Entertainment is to have former Aristocrat Leisure Ltd chief executive Gary Garton as its new chairman after John Hewson resigned yesterday, only six months after the company was floated. The resignation of fellow director Carmel Travers was also announced yesterday, but despite this, chief executive Karl O'Farrel says the company is improving. Page 21.

CSR, Australia's largest timber producer, is expecting to add A$800 million in shareholder value to its timber division after failing to attract a buyer for the whole business. Managing director Geoff Kells says failure to find a buyer has led to cost-cuting in the division. page 21.

The Australian Stock Exchange believes Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd may be in breach of the continuous disclosure rules, after not informing the market last week that it may pull-out of a A$342 million deal to buy management contracts atthe Sydney Harbour Casino. When asked last week of his intentions, Packer said no decision was made, but then announced on the weekend the deal was off. Page 22.

In his first public speech since becoming managing director of David Jones Ltd in March Peter Wilkinson said lifting the performance of the retail chain in a time of declining retail consumption was a challenge. He said Australian Bureau of Statistics figres estimate a further drop in retail sales of 1.5 per cent in the next five years. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Shares in Perth-based miner Golden Valley Mines fell almost 30 per cent yesterday following the release of a damning report on the Busang "gold" deposit in Indonesia. Golden Valley, which holds a 95 per cent stake in Indonesian firm PT Krueng Gasui - the holder of a 10 per cent in the Busang I deposit, shed 14 cents to 38 cents as it became the immediate Australian casualty of the Busang fraud. Page 21.

Colonial Ltd spokesman Simon Morgan said yesterday Colonial and its share registry, KPMG Registries, had received thousands of applications from would-be investors after the Australian Securities Commission last week forced the bancassurance group to reopn its float until 5pm today. Page 22.

Speaking in Newcastle yesterday, BHP managing director John Prescott said the ACTU's proposed 24-hour nationwide strike by steelworkers on May 15 was "very regrettable", and would not deter the company from closing the Newcastle steelworks in 1999, causing the loss of 2,500 jobs. Page 23.

Speaking during Australian Fashion Week in Sydney yesterday, Peter Wilkinson, the new chief executive of up-market retailer David Jones Ltd, said the company would go "back to the future" and utilise its reputation of impeccable service and quality to postion itself as a vital player in the retail industry. Page 23.

CSR Ltd managing director Geoff Kells has revealed the company has abandoned plans to sell its A$1 billion timber division after an international tender failed to produce a bid at CSR's asking price. The company will instead begin a restructuring and cost cutting plan to take at least A$60 million in yearly costs out of the business during the next two years. Page 23.

Following the success of its Myer Sports store and the launch of its Myer Electric stores later this month, retail giant Coles Myer has announced plans to open three new "category killer" stores - large outlets specialising in a single range of goods - as part of an ongoing revamp of its department store business. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking on the opening day of Mercedes Australian Fashion Week yesterday, Peter Wilkinson, the new chief executive of upmarket retailer David Jones, signalled he would slow down the company's push into private label goods as part of an overhaul of operatons to lift profitability. Page 25.

The Institute of Chartered Accountants warned yesterday the Federal Government's proposed 15 per cent superannuation surcharge, which doubles the 15 per cent tax on employer superannuation contributions to 30 per cent on gross incomes of A$85,000, may seethe 30,000 employees who face retrenchment by BHP, the ABC and Telstra suffer a 15 per cent cut in their redundancy packages. Page 25.

The money market has reacted strongly to the news that Tuesday's Federal Budget may reduce the underlying deficit by A$2 billion, increasing the chance of a balanced Budget by July 1999. The deficit is likely to be reduced to A$1.5 billion, with the help of anticipated economic growth. Page 25.

John Hewson has quit as chairman of video group Network Entertainment, a move which follows the resignations of directors Carmel Travers and Bonita Boezeman. It is believed Hewson quit after a disagreement with managing director Karl O'Farrel. Network Entertainment has faced financial difficulties since a poor trading performance in December 1996, and a decision to break contracts with two Hollywood film studios. Page 27.

Australian Stock Exchange deputy managing director, markets and settlements, Angus Richards said because of the lack of companies switching to uncertificated issue-sponsored share registries, the move to a three-day settlement deadline for share transactions has been delayed to next year. The ASX had hoped to move from the current five-day system to the three-day alternative by late this year. Page 27.

Building materials and sugar group CSR has been reviewing its timber division since March, which will be subject to cost-cutting for the next two years after CSR failed to find a buyer for it. The division attracted bids from many sources but none, accordng to managing director Geoff Kells, were acceptable. Page 27.
THE AGE

In a move which comes as Swiss financier Jurg Bollag risks a three-month jail term to remain silent on his financial links with Alan Bond, Andrew Tuohy, the head of the three-year Operation Oxide investigation into whether Bond concealed assets from his bankruptcy creditors, has resigned. Page B1.

In a surprise decision which comes after an international tender for CSR's A$1 billion timber division, the company, Australia's biggest timber group, has decided not to sell and is preparing to strip out at least A$30 million in costs each year for several years. Page B3.

As the Queensland Cabinet prepares to hand down its decision on whether to provide its share of the A$90 million compensation package that will allow the A$1.1 billion Century Zinc mine in the north of the State to proceed, the mining giant has asked for one-day extension to complete an agreement with Aborigines who have delayed the project for three years. Page B3.

Responding to comments made on the weekend by Crown casino chairman Lloyd Williams, Sydney Harbour Casino chief executive Neil Gamble said yesterday he does not envisage any merger with the Melbourne casino and denied that he has held talks with Crown offcials to discuss the issue. Page B3.

KPMG associate director Johanna Plante, a former head of Telstra's access and local telephony operations and a former commissioner of the Trade Practices Commission, said yesterday the opening of Australian telecommunications markets was a "time bomb" that could see new entrants shake the entire industry. Page B3.

As part of an overhaul to operations aimed to boost profitability, David Jones' new chief executive Peter Wilkinson yesterday rejected his predecessor Chris Tideman's decision to lift the sales volume of the retailer's own label apparel business from 13 to 28 per cent, saying he thought that increase was "too quick". Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
